refusal_rule: A refused job goes back to pending uncounted and the runner keeps going. Only a REQUEST rejection (every lane that ran answered HTTP 400/413/422 or an ambiguous body: KeyError/JSONDecodeError) can ever be charged, and only when a LATER job in the same run is answered. Any other refusal (429, 5xx, timeout, transport, unavailable, gate) is never charged. outage_after_refusals refusals in a row with no answer (or two or more when the queue ends) are a lane outage: the outage breaker opens, nobody is charged. An outage after answers in the same run is a flap: the next runs halve their volume per flap until a run ends cleanly.
probe_rule: While the outage breaker is open the probe is jobs[min(trips, n-1)] (rotating), then the head decides.
